name: Lordicon
tagline: 48,100+ hand-animated icons in Lottie, GIF, SVG, and more, with a web component, React package, and API
description:
Lordicon is a library of more than 48,100 animated icons in three families: Wired, System, and Doodle. The team sketches each icon, draws it in Figma, and animates it by hand in After Effects. You change colors, stroke, speed, size, and the animation state, such as intro, hover, morph, or loop. Then you export Lottie, GIF, MP4, SVG, PNG, WebP, APNG, AEP, or MOGRT files.

About 9,700 icons are free for commercial use with attribution. PRO costs $8 a month billed yearly and removes the attribution. On the web, the @lordicon/element web component and the @lordicon/react package play the icons. A Figma plugin, a WordPress plugin, Webflow docs, and a developer API complete the set.
pricing_detail: Free: about 9,700 icons for commercial use with attribution and one icon collection. PRO: $8 a month billed yearly or $16 billed monthly, 38,300 more icons, and no attribution. Team PRO: $39 a month billed yearly for up to 50 members. Downloaded icons stay usable after a subscription ends.
agent_guidance:
Read lordicon.com/licenses before you ship a free icon. The free license follows CC BY-ND 4.0 with changes: commercial use is allowed, but you must credit Lordicon.

On a web page, install @lordicon/element and use the lord-icon element. In React, use @lordicon/react. Pick the animation state that fits the moment: hover for buttons, loop for a wait, and intro for an empty state. Keep animated icons for key moments, not for every icon in a list.
why_it_matters: It is one of the largest libraries of hand-animated icons, with export formats for the web, mobile apps, video, and motion design tools.
tier_reason: A large, consistent, hand-animated library with good tooling. Most icons need PRO, and free use needs attribution.
notable_for: Lottie, GIF, MP4, SVG, AEP, and MOGRT export
attribution required on the free plan
evidence: Checked https://lordicon.com/, /pricing, /licenses, /api-developers, /docs, and the npm registry on 2026-10-09. The home page reported 48,100+ icons, 9,700+ free icons, and the export formats. The pricing page listed Free, PRO at $8 a month billed yearly, and Team PRO at $39 a month billed yearly. npm lists @lordicon/element 3.0.2 and @lordicon/react 2.0.0, both MIT, published on 2026-10-07. The site has no llms.txt. Source tweet: https://x.com/DevDsgn/status/2108552027962036228.

name: Flaticon Animated Icons
tagline: 57,000+ animated icons in Lottie JSON, GIF, MP4, SVG, and After Effects formats, free with attribution
description:
Flaticon Animated Icons is the animated section of Flaticon, a library of more than 18 million icons. The section lists more than 57,000 animated icons in many design styles. GIF, MP4, and PNG files are free. Lottie JSON and After Effects files are editable, and SVG, EPS, and PSD files give static vectors.

Free use needs a credit line to the author and Flaticon. Premium costs 8.25 USD a month and removes the attribution. The live site blocked automated access during the check, so this record uses the archived page from 2026-10-07.
pricing_detail: Free downloads need attribution to the author and Flaticon. Premium costs 8.25 USD a month and gives access to more than 18 million icons with no attribution.
agent_guidance:
Check the attribution rule before you use a free icon, and add the credit line that Flaticon gives with each download. Prefer the Lottie JSON file for apps and sites, because you can change its colors and size. Use GIF or MP4 only where a Lottie player is not possible.

An agent cannot read the live site, because it blocks automated requests. Pick icons in a browser, then give the agent the downloaded files.
why_it_matters: It is a very large source of animated icons in many styles, with free GIF and MP4 files.
tier_reason: A very large catalog, but free use needs attribution, the styles vary, and the site blocks automated access.
notable_for: Lottie JSON and After Effects files
attribution required on the free plan
evidence: The live page https://www.flaticon.com/animated-icons returned HTTP 403 to curl, to crawler user agents, and to headless Chromium on 2026-10-09. The facts come from the Wayback Machine copy of 2026-10-07. Its title reported 57,000+ animated icons, and the page listed Lottie JSON, GIF, MP4, SVG, and After Effects formats and Premium at 8.25 USD a month. Source tweet: https://x.com/DevDsgn/status/2108552027962036228.

name: All SVG Icons
tagline: 380,000+ free SVG icons from 238 open-source packs, with free SVG tools and an MCP server for agents
description:
All SVG Icons is a free search site for more than 380,000 SVG icons from 238 open-source icon packs, such as Material Design Icons, Tabler, Lucide, and Font Awesome Free. You copy raw SVG, JSX, or Base64 code or download PNG files, with no sign-up. Each pack keeps its own license, and its pack page shows it. An Animated collection groups spinners, loaders, and animated SVG icons.

The site also has free browser tools: a logo maker, an SVG optimizer, a sprite maker, a favicon generator, and a 3D avatar builder. An MCP server lets an agent search icons and fetch SVG markup, with 20 free calls a day and a paid plan for more. The site marks itself as beta.
pricing_detail: The site and its tools are free with no sign-up. The MCP server allows 20 free calls a day after a Google or GitHub sign-in. MCP Pro costs $29 one time for the first 50 buyers, then $49 for the next 50, and later $9 a month or $79 a year.
agent_guidance:
Read allsvgicons.com/llms.txt first. Search across packs, then open the pack page and check its license before you copy an icon. Some packs need attribution to the original author, not to All SVG Icons.

Keep one pack per product, so stroke width and corner style stay consistent. For an agent, the MCP server at i.allsvgicons.com/mcp returns SVG markup by prefix and name.
why_it_matters: It puts most open-source icon packs in one search, with license data and agent access.
tier_reason: Broad, useful, and ready for agents, but a new beta site that collects other packs and shows ads.
notable_for: SVG, JSX, PNG, and Base64 output
evidence: Checked https://allsvgicons.com/, /llms.txt, /mcp/, and /terms/ on 2026-10-09. The home page reported 380,000+ icons in 238+ libraries, an Animated collection, and SVG, PNG, JSX, and Base64 output. The MCP page reported 380,089 icons, four tools, 20 free calls a day, and the paid plans. The terms state that each pack keeps its original license. Source tweet: https://x.com/DevDsgn/status/2108552027962036228.

name: useAnimations
tagline: 298 free MIT animated Lottie icons with a React package, a shadcn registry, and an agent catalog
description:
useAnimations is a free library of 298 animated icons drawn on 24 and 32 px artboards. Each icon has a Lottie JSON file with a direct URL, static SVG files, and a ZIP package. Icons play on a loop, a click, or a hover.

The react-useanimations package plays the icons in React, and a shadcn registry adds one icon as a component. The docs cover plain HTML, Vue, Svelte, Angular, iOS, and Android. Everything uses the MIT license, with no attribution required.
pricing_detail: Free. All files and the React package use the MIT license, and attribution is not required.
agent_guidance:
Fetch useanimations.com/icons.json to pick an icon by keyword and interaction type. In React, install react-useanimations, or add one icon with the shadcn registry.

On a plain page, load the Lottie JSON from its direct URL with the lottie-web light build. The error and twitter icons need the full build. Recolor the icons to match your design system, and keep the motion for state changes.
why_it_matters: It is a small, MIT-licensed animated icon set that an agent can search and install without an account.
tier_reason: Free, MIT, and well documented for agents and for many platforms. The set is small at 298 icons.
evidence: Checked https://useanimations.com/, /llms.txt, /icons.json, /r/registry.json, /documentation.md, and /licencing-and-terms on 2026-10-09. icons.json lists 298 icons. The terms state the MIT license with no attribution required. The GitHub API reports 1,247 stars and a last push on 2026-10-08. npm lists react-useanimations 2.10.0 under MIT. Source tweet: https://x.com/DevDsgn/status/2108552027962036228.

name: SVGator
tagline: Online SVG animation editor that exports animated SVG, Lottie, GIF, and video, with an MCP for AI agents
description:
SVGator is a browser-based editor for SVG animation. You import or draw vector art, then animate it on a timeline with keyframes, morphing, motion paths, and easing, without code. Exports include animated SVG with CSS or JavaScript, Lottie JSON, React Native and Flutter files, GIF, WebP, APNG, and video.

A Player API controls interactive animations on click, on hover, or from code. SVGator has Figma and WordPress plugins and an official MCP that builds animations from a text prompt. The Free plan exports static SVG only. Animated exports start with the Starter plan at $20 a month billed yearly.
pricing_detail: Free: the full editor and unlimited static SVG exports. Starter: $20 a month billed yearly for animated SVG, Lottie, React Native, and Flutter export and the Player API. Pro: $24 a month billed yearly for unlimited animations and video and GIF export. Team: $27 per seat a month billed yearly, from 3 seats.
agent_guidance:
Use SVGator when a designer wants a hand-tuned SVG animation, such as an animated logo, icon, or loader, without code. Export animated SVG for the web, because it stays small and sharp at any size. Use the Player API for click or hover control.

Check which plan includes the export format you need before you start a project. With the MCP, an agent drafts the animation from a prompt, and the result stays editable in SVGator.
why_it_matters: It turns static vector art into small animated files for web and app interfaces, without code.
tier_reason: A mature editor with many export formats and an MCP. Animated exports need a paid plan.
notable_for: animated SVG with CSS or JavaScript
evidence: Checked https://www.svgator.com/, /pricing, /mcp-for-ai-animations, and /help on 2026-10-09. The home page listed the animators, the export formats, and the Figma and WordPress plugins. The pricing page listed Free, Starter at $20, Pro at $24, and Team at $27 per seat, all a month billed yearly. The MCP page describes prompt-based animation that stays editable in the editor. The site has no llms.txt. Source tweet: https://x.com/DevDsgn/status/2108552027962036228.
